description:
Background: JMAP-x2gd.13 closed the handler-side enforcement of the
(account, chatId) uniqueness invariant on ReadPosition. The handler now
rejects sequential and intra-batch duplicate creates via an alreadyExists
SetError naming the canonical existing id.

What is NOT closed: two concurrent ReadPosition/set requests for the
same chatId can both pass the handler's pre-check before either
calls create_object, then both can call create_object, then both
records land in storage. The MemoryBackend's generic create_object
in src/memory.rs has no chatId-uniqueness check.

The handler-side pre-check is sufficient for the retry-storm case
(serial duplicate requests) but not for the concurrent-write case
(two clients submitting in parallel).

Why this is filed as P3 not P2: the kit's policy is backend-canonical
for permission and invariant enforcement (workspace AGENTS.md
"Caller identity (foundation seam)"). The reference MemoryBackend
is feature-gated, explicitly demonstration-quality, and its single-
lock-on-create_object pattern actually serializes writes — concurrent
creates against the in-memory backend already cannot race in
practice because each call acquires the same Mutex. The race window
exists conceptually but cannot be triggered against the kit's
reference backend.

Production backends that use a real database (the kit's intended
production deployment shape) MUST enforce a unique constraint on
(account_id, chat_id) at the storage layer. The ChatBackend trait
does not currently communicate this requirement.

Two action paths:

1. Document the contract: extend the ChatBackend::create_object
   doc (or add a per-type contract section in the ReadPosition
   handler module-doc) explicitly stating 'backends MUST enforce
   (account, chatId) uniqueness atomically with the create; the
   handler pre-check is defense-in-depth only'.

2. Type-dispatch in MemoryBackend.create_object: when TYPE_NAME ==
   ReadPosition::TYPE_NAME, scan the existing records for a
   matching chatId before insertion. Same approach extends to
   future singleton-by-foreign-key types.

Path (1) is the minimum honest fix; path (2) makes the reference
impl a faithful demonstration of the production contract. Both
are pre-1.0 safe.

Engineering basis: the JMAP-x2gd.13 description explicitly listed
the unclosed backend-side enforcement as the second half of the
fix sketch ('AND in MemoryBackend.create_object<ReadPosition>,
enforce the uniqueness atomically'). The handler-side commit
c5aac30 closes the first half.
title: ReadPosition (account, chatId) uniqueness: concurrent-create race window unclosed at backend layer
